Observation 2 There is no definition of ‘coherent antenna port groups’ in the RAN1 specs, although coherent UL MIMO operation applies within antenna port groups according to the RAN1 specs. Observation 3 Whether a value ‘first’ or ‘second’ for tpmi-FullPwrCodebook2-r18 refers to antenna port group 0 or 1 is not stated in 38.306, although one *may* guess that ‘first’ refers to antenna port group 0. Observation 4 While the UE can determine which TPMIs are associated with a port group, 38.306 and the RAN1 specs do not state that all TPMIs associated with a port group must deliver full power. Observation 5 The current specification’s description using only antenna port groups to define TPMI groups may require the UE to report full power Mode 1 TPMIs, and so is insufficient/incorrect. Proposal 7 Clarify that “across all serving cells” means “across all serving cells in the band”. Proposal 8 A UE that supports FG 45-1a can perform L1 measurements on any band.

case of high mobility, e.g., in v=120km/h. Proposal 3: Together with NR-SSS, the sequence-based NR-DMRS/TSS should be considered to improve the channel estimation of NR-PBCH demodulation. Transmission schemes and the number of antenna ports We assume the NR-SSS has same number of antenna port(s) as NR-PBCH and the NR-SSS is sent on the same antenna port as that of NR-PBCH. Assuming same tx power and 2x2 antenna configuration, different transmit diversity are compared based on simulation. Alt.1: Two antenna port based SFBC Alt.2: Single antenna port based transmission scheme In Atl1, the channel estimation uses the NR-SSS+NR-DMRS/TSS designed for 2 antenna ports. But in Alt2, the channel estimation uses the NR-SSS+NR-DMRS/TSS designed for 1 antenna port. The use of tx diversity schemes is transparent to the UEs, which only observes single radio link with equivalent combined channel. In the simulation, we apply precoder cycling across SSS and PBCH symbols within each radio frames and change the precoder cycling parameters over multiple radio frames, such as [1 1]T, [1 -1]T, [1 j]T, [1 –j]T. The different tx diversity schemes are compared in Figure 3-(a) under channel delay spread of 100ns and 1000ns on 4GHz, and in Figure 3-(b) under channel delay spread of 100ns on 30GHz frequency, respectively. The SISO performance is also given as a reference. The other detailed simulation assumption is given in Appendix A. In Figure 3, we use the IFDM of PBCH and DMRS/TSS multiplexing as illustrated comparison. The coherent combining over 40ms TTI for PBCH is used for the analysis of the worst-case in terms of coverage. Since the 2-port SFBC requires orthogonal RS to get respective channel estimation on each antenna, Alt1 performs worse than Alt2 due to higher channel estimation error for NR-PBCH demodulation. (a) 4GHz (b) 30GHz Figure 3: BLER performances of NR-PBCH with various Tx schemes Proposal 4: Transparent tx diversity scheme on 1 antenna port (e.g., precoder cycling) is used for NR-PBCH transmission. Periodicity and coding rate of NR-PBCH demodulation In LTE design, the MIB uses a fixed schedule with a periodicity of 40 ms and repetitions made within 40 ms. The first transmission of the MIB is scheduled in subframe #0 of radio frames for which the SFN mod 4 = 0, and repetitions are scheduled in subframe #0 of all other radio frames. MIB is self-decodable per transmission, but UE is allowed to decode the MIB across the repetitions. Considering the four-time repetitions, the PBCH coding rate is 1/48. A similar principle can be considered for NR as well. Proposal 5: The NR-PBCH periodicity is [40]ms and the coding rate of NR-PBCH considering repetitions within the NR-PBCH window of [40]ms shall be around 1/48.

In this paper, we discussed the CSI-RS based RRM measurements and the TRP/beam synchronization signals as the Tertiary Synchronization Signals (TSS). Based on the discussion, we have the following proposals: Proposal 1: The CSI-RS RRM measurements should be configured by network; Proposal 2: Beam grouping information should be signalled to UE together with the CSI-RS configuration for RRM measurements. Proposal 3: Introduce the TRP/beam-SS as the Tertiary Synchronization Signal (TSS) for each Beam or TRP with a cell for UE autonomous detection and channel tracking of each TRP/beam. TRP/beam-SS is also used as the antenna port to be QCLed with each CSI-RS port for RRM measurements. Proposal 4: Design the TRP/beam-SS based on the M-sequences with the similar approach as LTE SSS.

In NR, however, the periodicity will be decided one of two values 10 and 20ms, and any value will be longer than LTE. Therefore, NR-PBCH might be included in every SS block. If similar payload size with LTE is considered, two OFDM symbols for NR-PBCH will be enough. It should be studied further considering NR-PBCH design and periodicity of SS burst set. The following is defined in RAN4 TSs [1], [2], related to pi/2-BPSK modulation-based transmission, ….. For Pi/2 BPSK modulation the UE shall be allowed to employ spectral shaping and the shaping filter shall be restricted so that the impulse response of the shaping filter itself shall meet │ãt(t,0)│ ≥ │ãt(t, τ)│ ∀τ ≠ 0 20log10│ãt(t,τ)│< -15 dB 1< τ < M - 1, where│ãt(t, τ)│=IDFT{│ãt(t,f)│ejφ (t,f)}, f is the frequency of the M allocated subcarriers , ã(t,f) and φ(t,f) are the amplitude and phase response. ….. The above mentions that pi/2-BPSK transmissions can be spectrum shaped before transmission. In Rel-16, pi/2-BPSK based low PAPR reference signals were introduced in RAN1 TS [3]. Although pi/2-BPSK PUSCH uses single layer transmission, the RS is defined to be used as per signalled antenna port wherein the RS occupies either even or odd RS subcarrier locations. While PUSCH data can be spectrum shaped for “all” subcarriers, the RS undergoes spectrum shaping only for a portion of the subcarriers based on the antenna port. In [4], it has been shown that unless the TS specifies the relation between PUSCH data spectrum shaping filter and PUSCH RS spectrum shaping filter, the receiver will experience a performance loss. This loss can be mitigated by defining the relationship between PUSCH data and RS filtering process. In RAN1 and RAN4 it is understood that the potential pi/2-BPSK spectrum shaping is an implementation specific feature. Nevertheless, merely a relation between the PUSCH data filter and PUSCH RS filter shall be specified in RAN1 TS. With this additional clarification in the RAN1 spec, the pi/2-BPSK feature shall be considered a complete specification. Proposal: The following must be captured in 5.2.3 in TS 38.211

Proposal 3: The RS used for RSRP measurement (i.e., SSS + potentially PBCH DMRS) can be used as IMR for SSS based RS-SINR. Proposal 4: The CSI-RS REs used for the RSRP measurement can be used as IMR for SSS based RS-SINR. Proposal 5: CSI-RSSI measurement BW is identical to configured CSI-RS measurement BW. Proposal 6: Measurement bandwidth used in SS-RSRQ definition is up to UE implementation with the limitation that corresponding measurement accuracy requirements have to be fulfilled. Proposal 7: Proposed to add the following description to RSRP definition: If the receiver beamforming is in use by the UE, RSRP shall be measured based on the combined signal from antenna elements corresponding to a given receiver branch.
